claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.5 underlined words in a general format are REQUIRED words and non-underlined uppercase words are OPTIONAL. Dropping the underlining makes IS, THAN and TO look mandatory, so the falsely-restrictive reading rejects legal source such as 'IF A NOT GREATER B', 'IF A GREATER OR EQUAL B' and 'IF A NOT EQUAL B' — exactly the lossy-toward-restrictive failure mode this sweep targets. The transcription already has a convention for this (<u>...</u>, used in ~97 places, e.g. line 9691 '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1'), so this figure is simply missing it. Secondarily, the PDF delimiter is a brace (choose exactly one, mandatory) and the box-drawing rectangle does not distinguish brace from bracket.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently verified against the 300 dpi render of PDF page 204 (printed page 174) at E:/Temp/specrecon/v204/spec_p204.png, magnified crops fig_zoom.png and delims.png, and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8850-8866 (workunit page-204.md lines 6-20).

GLYPHS I ACTUALLY SEE IN THE PDF, row by row (underlines are unambiguous at 8x magnification):
 1. IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO — separate underlines under GREATER, under OR, under EQUAL. IS, THAN and TO carry no rule.
 2. IS >= — no underline.
 3. IS NOT LESS THAN — underlines under NOT and under LESS only.
 4. IS NOT < — underline under NOT only.
 5. IS LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO — underlines under LESS, OR, EQUAL only.
 6. IS <= — no underline.
 7. IS NOT GREATER THAN — underlines under NOT and GREATER only.
 8. IS NOT > — underline under NOT only.
 9. IS NOT EQUAL TO — underlines under NOT and EQUAL only.
10. IS NOT = — underline under NOT only.
11. IS <> — no underline.
The claimed underline pattern matches the printed page exactly on all 11 rows; the claim does not misquote the PDF.

DELIMITER: cropping the left and right delimiter columns alone (delims.png) shows a tall glyph with curved terminals at top and bottom and a distinct mid-height cusp level with the 'IS <=' row, on BOTH sides — i.e. a printed '{' and a mirrored '}'. It is a brace pair, not a bracket pair and not a rectangle. Per 5.2.6.3 that means exactly one alternative shall be selected and the choice is mandatory.

MARKDOWN: the transcription is a plain box-drawing rectangle. I confirmed by reading the raw source that the eleven lines inside the fence are plain uppercase text — no <u> tags, no bold, no other emphasis carrier, and the fence is a code block so no markup could survive inside it anyway. All underline information is gone. The claimed markdown text matches the file byte for byte apart from the box width.

NOT EXPLAINABLE AS FURNITURE: this is not reflow, hyphenation, a page break or a wrapping artifact — the eleven alternatives are all present and correctly ordered; what is missing is the required/optional distinction that the printed page encodes purely typographically.

NO COMPENSATING NOTE: this transcription carries two established mechanisms for preserving this information — inline <u>...</u> (97 lines use it) and a '> **Figure notes (...)**' blockquote that spells out which words are underlined and whether the delimiter is a brace or a bracket (used on ~25+ figures, e.g. lines 3407, 3545, 4871, 6178). Neither is applied here. There is no figure-notes blockquote for 8.7.5.1 at all, so nothing elsewhere in the file restores the lost distinction.

CONSEQUENCE CHECK: with the underlines gone, a reader/implementer taking the box literally would require IS, THAN and TO, rejecting the legal forms 'A NOT GREATER B', 'A GREATER OR EQUAL B', 'A NOT EQUAL B', 'A LESS OR EQUAL B'. That is the falsely-restrictive direction. The claim's consequence argument holds.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM'S RATIONALE (not to either source): the convention is not in 5.2.5. In this document 5.2.5 is 'Level numbers'. The governing subclauses are 5.2.2 Keywords ('shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats … required'), 5.2.3 Optional words ('uppercase words that are not underlined … may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics'), restated at 8.3.2.4.2/8.3.2.4.3, and 5.2.6.3 Braces for the delimiter point. The finding itself is unaffected.

ADJACENT (out of scope for this page but same defect): the Format 1 (simple-relational-operator) figure immediately above, transcribed at the end of page 203, is likewise stripped of underlining and is rendered with '⌐ ¬ | L ┘' pseudo-bracket characters, which additionally reads as a BRACKET (optional) rather than the printed brace.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with one citation correction. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8850-8866 transcribe the 8.7.5.1 Format 2 (extended-relational-operator) general format as a plain box-drawing rectangle containing eleven unstyled uppercase lines. The printed page (PDF p.204 = printed p.174) shows the same eleven alternatives enclosed in a BRACE pair ('{' … '}', mid-height cusps visible on both sides), with per-word underlining on ten of the eleven rows: GREATER/OR/EQUAL; (none); NOT/LESS; NOT; LESS/OR/EQUAL; (none); NOT/GREATER; NOT; NOT/EQUAL; NOT; (none). IS, THAN and TO are never underlined. Per 5.2.2 (Keywords — underlined = required) and 5.2.3 (Optional words — not underlined = optional at the user's option), the transcription loses the required/optional distinction and reads as though IS, THAN and TO were mandatory, which would falsely reject legal source such as 'IF A NOT GREATER B', 'IF A GREATER OR EQUAL B', 'IF A LESS OR EQUAL B' and 'IF A NOT EQUAL B'. Per 5.2.6.3, the brace also encodes a mandatory choose-exactly-one, which the neutral rectangle does not convey. The claim's rationale miscited the convention as 5.2.5; 5.2.5 is 'Level numbers'. Fix: re-render the figure with the brace delimiter and <u>…</u> on the ten underlined-word rows, or add the standard '> **Figure notes (…)**' blockquote used by ~25 other figures in this file; the same defect affects the Format 1 figure transcribed at the end of page 203, which is additionally rendered with bracket-like characters instead of a brace.
